title: Identity, organizations, policy, preferences, and white-label branding
objective: Keep user, organization, policy, preference, and brand authority coherent from first sign-in through enterprise identity governance.

obligations.title: Managed surfaces project one server-authenticated actor identity
obligations.residualRisk: A hard-coded, browser-supplied, or stale actor can be displayed or written to audit evidence as though it were the authenticated user.

obligations.title: Organization role authority comes from the exact actor membership row
obligations.residualRisk: A fixed role, fallback role, owner shortcut, invalid role value, or mismatched membership can grant capabilities the actor does not hold.

obligations.title: Managed preferences persist under authenticated account authority
obligations.residualRisk: A managed user can be shown demo-local or another user's preferences and receive a false success when durable persistence fails.

obligations.title: Demo identity and storage cannot authorize a managed account
obligations.residualRisk: A demo query, local storage record, or demo session can bypass managed authentication or leak into production actor and preference state.

obligations.title: Sign-out succeeds only after server session revocation succeeds
obligations.residualRisk: The interface can report a successful sign-out while the server cookie or provider session remains valid.

obligations.title: Foreign tenant identifiers fail closed before reads or writes
obligations.residualRisk: A caller can combine an authenticated identity with a foreign organization, team, member, invite, or preference identifier.

obligations.title: Organizations, delegated administration, and policy changes are tenant-safe under concurrency
obligations.residualRisk: Delegated administration can cross tenant boundaries or lose concurrent preference updates.

obligations.title: Enterprise identity, policy decisions, and brand changes are strongly authenticated and auditable
obligations.residualRisk: Password-only access and incomplete audit attribution cannot satisfy higher-assurance tenants.
